transport: One combined HDMI + USB cable to the GX device. HDMI carries video, USB carries touch input and power. No network interface of any kind.
refutedOnReview: REFUTED — not on the identity of the parts, but on the register-map claim itself, which is self-contradictory.  What checks out: - https://www.victronenergy.com/display-and-panels/gx-touch-50 exists and is a single page titled "GX Touch 50 & GX Touch 70" ("display accessories for our Cerbo GX"). It names BPP900455150 (GX Touch 50 Flush) and BPP900455170 (GX Touch 70 Flush) and carries drilling jigs for both Flush var
gotchas: This is a monitor, not a device. It renders the GX's local console over HDMI and sends touch events back over USB. There is nothing to poll and nothing to command. It appears in the catalogue only so a future reader does not spend an afternoon looking for its protocol.
It requires a GX with an HDMI port. The Nucleo GX has none — Victron's Nucleo manual points at an Android GX WiFi Display instead. Do not pair a GX Touch with a Nucleo GX.
Anything a GX Touch shows, Modbus TCP or MQTT already exposes. Adding one changes what a person at the cabin sees, not what Cabin Hub can read.
